question: The standard empiric regimen for acute bacterial meningitis in a child older than 1 month includes ceftriaxone, vancomycin, AND dexamethasone as adjunctive therapy.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Ceftriaxone + vancomycin is the recommended empiric antibiotic combination in children >1 month; vancomycin covers the possibility of penicillin/cephalosporin-resistant pneumococcus. Dexamethasone is given adjunctively to attenuate the inflammatory cascade. Neonates (0–28 days) receive a different regimen: ampicillin + gentamicin or ampicillin + cefotaxime.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. In children >1 month with suspected bacterial meningitis, the combination of ceftriaxone (covers pneumococcus and meningococcus) plus vancomycin (covers penicillin-resistant pneumococcus) is standard empiric antibiotic therapy. Dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg every 6 hours for 4 days is given as adjunctive therapy (ideally 15–20 minutes before or with the first antibiotic dose) to reduce inflammation and lower the risk of neurological sequelae, particularly hearing loss.
